description: "Tell me about X" / "research Acme" / "brief me on Tesla" / "what does Apple do" / "company profile for Microsoft" / "give me the rundown on NVDA" / "everything you know about $TICKER" — full cross-source profile of a US public company in ONE parallel call. ALWAYS PREFER over chaining single-pack SEC/XBRL/news lookups when the user asks for a holistic view. Fans out across SEC EDGAR, XBRL, USPTO patents, federal contracts (USAspending), FDA-licensed biologics (Purple Book), H-1B hiring (DOL LCA), news and GLEIF, and returns: cik + company_name (+ resolved_from/resolved_to when `value` was a name); recent_filings (up to 5 with pipeworx://edgar/company/{cik}/filings/{accession} URIs); fundamentals (the latest ANNUAL Revenues, NetIncomeLoss, Cash, diluted EPS, capex and operating cash flow, each with its period_end, SEC form and the accession of the filing it came from — plus EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, which is the newest COVER-PAGE share count the filer has published rather than an annual one, so its period_end is a cover date after the quarter closed and it is the right per-share denominator; a filer tagging a fallback concept appears under the name of that tag instead, e.g. PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets instead of PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment); patents (USPTO PatentsView API sunset May 2025 — soft-fails until reactivated); federal_contracts (USAspending awards where the company is the recipient); fda_products (FDA-licensed biologics — vaccines, cell/gene therapies — from the Purple Book; a company with only small-molecule/generic drugs will show none here, that is expected, not a failure); hiring (H-1B sponsorship volume + salary range from DOL LCA filings); recent news mentions via GDELT→GNews fallback; LEI via GLEIF. `sources_used` / `sources_failed` say which of these actually returned data for THIS company — an empty section is a real "no data", not a bug. `sources_skipped` is the third state: a leg we deliberately did NOT run, each entry carrying a `reason` token and a plain-English `detail` (the Purple Book is skipped for a filer SEC classifies outside the life-science SIC bands, since it lists only 351(a)/(k) biologics licence holders). Pass a ticker ("AAPL"), zero-padded CIK ("0000320193"), OR a company name ("Moderna") — names now resolve via SEC EDGAR's company-name match; a private company (no CIK/ticker) returns resolved:false with an explicit `notes` line, not a bare failure. `type` accepts "company" or "ticker" interchangeably — both take the same `value` shapes above.

country.description: OPTIONAL ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 of the business register you mean ("NO", "FI", "GB", "JP", "FR", "EE", "BR"). Only affects a NAME lookup, and is often what separates the company you mean from a US namesake. When a name resolves to a register entity with no CIK, the SEC/CIK-keyed sections are reported under `sources_skipped` with reason `not_queried` — they were never asked, which is not the same as having failed.

type.description: "company" or "ticker" — both are accepted and behave identically; `value` can be a ticker, CIK, or company name either way. person/place coming soon.

value.description: Ticker (e.g., "AAPL"), zero-padded CIK (e.g., "0000320193"), or company name (e.g., "Moderna"). A NAME now resolves through the national business registers as well as SEC EDGAR, so a non-US company returns its register identity and record rather than `resolved: false`.
